meta.disclaimer: Educational illustration only. Not financial, tax, legal, or investment advice. Figures are approximate, lag official releases, and can change. No endorsement of any institution, policy, or political entity is implied.

level_1.name: Individual Large Capital Holders
level_1.description: Public-facing owners and founders. Subject to market pricing, regulatory frameworks, and asset revaluation. They hold claims on productive assets but do not set the overall cost of capital.

level_2.name: Large Institutional Asset Managers
level_2.description: Entities managing multi-trillion portfolios of passive and active assets. Collectively hold substantial voting influence across major listed corporations through aggregated client capital.

level_3.name: Monetary Authorities & Sovereign Issuers
level_3.description: Central banks and related sovereign entities that influence interest rates, liquidity provision, and systemic backstops. They shape the conditions under which all other capital operates.

stratification_tiers.name: High-Earner Labor Tier
stratification_tiers.description: Upper wage or professional income still primarily dependent on active work. High marginal tax rates apply to labor income before expenses.

stratification_tiers.name: Income & Wealth Top Percentile
stratification_tiers.description: Thresholds around the top 1% of tax returns by AGI and corresponding household net-worth entry points drawn from survey and distributional accounts.

stratification_tiers.name: Large Private Capital Holders
stratification_tiers.description: Ownership of equity, real assets, and intellectual property that compounds independently of continuous labor input.

sources: IRS Statistics of Income (SOI) Division — Individual income tax returns by percentile (AGI floors).
Federal Reserve Distributional Financial Accounts (DFA) — Quarterly wealth distribution by percentile.
Federal Reserve Survey of Consumer Finances (SCF) — Triennial household balance-sheet microdata.
U.S. Census Bureau Current Population Survey (CPS) / Income in the United States reports — Median and distributional income.
Bureau of Labor Statistics — Usual weekly earnings of full-time workers.
Piketty–Saez and World Inequality Database series — Historical capital vs. labor income shares.
Public company and fund reporting — Assets under management of large institutional managers.
data_integrity_notes: Income 1% threshold (~$748k AGI): Consistent with IRS Statistics of Income percentile tables (tax year 2023 data released 2026). Distinguishes tax-return AGI from pure wage income or CPS household measures.
Top 1% net-worth entry (~$13.7M–$16.5M range): Aligns with Federal Reserve Survey of Consumer Finances (2022) and subsequent distributional updates / analyses.
Median individual earnings ~$47k–$53k: Consistent with Census CPS and BLS earnings series.
Institutional AUM tier ($10T–$30T+): Reflects public reporting of the largest global asset managers.
Top 1% wealth share ~30%+ of total household net worth: Federal Reserve Distributional Financial Accounts.
